title: Candidate Continuity & Emergency Boarding Protocol (14-day)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc defines a short-form, repeatable protocol for candidate continuity and emergency boarding when we need to accelerate start timelines or recover from last-minute offer rollbacks, hiring freezes, or hardware delays. The focus is pragmatic: keep candidate experience high, protect hiring equity, and minimize operational friction for managers and infra.

When to use this protocol:
- Offer accepted but start date uncertain (e.g., visa, relocation delay).
- Immediate pro tem boarding required (project ramp, unexpected vacancy).
- Offer revoked or candidate rescinded and we must reassign commitments quickly.
- Hiring freeze triggers but work is critical for a short window.

Primary goals:
1) Provide a 14-day tactical window to onboard someone to be productive at a minimum viable scope.
2) Ensure security and compliance controls are respected (least privilege, audit log).
3) Preserve candidate goodwill and clear communications.
4) Create an automatic fallback loop to de-escalate if the situation changes.

Quick triage (first 24 hours) — people-ops checklist:
- Confirm trigger and decision owner: who authorized emergency boarding? (name + Slack/Email).
- Identify candidate(s) impacted and status (offer accepted, background complete, hardware delivered).
- Assign a single coordinator: People Ops lead for this case (POC).
- Notify hiring manager and assigned mentor.
- Open Jira ticket HR-1982 (template) and tag legal/compliance if offer terms change.
- Decide scope of access: minimum required services list (see Access matrix).
- Communicate to candidate: short transparent note (template below) within 12 hours.

14-day tactical onboarding plan (high-level):
Day 0-2: Safety + access
- Identity: Verify final ID and onboarding XR (if remote). Confirm offered legal paperwork.
- Access: Provision only the minimal set (git read-only, Slack, email, and ticketing). Use temporary role: "emergency-boarding-2w" with auto-expiry.
- Hardware: if no laptop available, enable cloud dev workstation (VM image 'swift-guest') and ensure VPN tokens.
- HR checklist: payroll setup, benefits deferred note, background check status filed.
- Mentor pairing confirmed and 1:1 scheduled for day 1.

Day 3-7: Ramp to MVF (Minimum Viable Focus)
- Identify 1–2 scope-bounded tickets (bug fix + small feature) that teach codebase flows and CI. Ticket size: ~2–8 hours.
- Mentor-led walkthrough: repo layout, deploy steps, local runbook, and safety/canary processes.
- Weekly micro-eval: quick feedback on blockers and any security concerns.
- Observability access: read-only dashboards; restrict production write or rollback.

Day 8-14: Transition or de-escalation
- Assess: can candidate continue (full onboarding) or should we pause/convert to contractor or withdraw? Criteria: background checks cleared, visa/relocation risk resolved, manager recommendation.
- If continuing: convert temporary roles to permanent roles, update IAM, schedule full security training, and place hardware reorder.
- If pausing: de-provision interactive access, retain read-only audit logs, provide clear exit communication and offer re-engagement plan.

Access matrix (minimal subset for 14-day window)
- Email account (required)
- Slack (general + team channels)
- GitHub: repo read + PR comments; push only to personal fork until day 8+
- CI/CD: view-only; no deploy tokens
- Production systems: NO access unless explicit manager exception and logged
- Cloud consoles: temporary limited role with auto-expiry (policy: 14d)
- Ticketing (Jira): create/edit for assigned tickets, not board admin

Communications templates (copy-paste, keep brief)
- Candidate initial note (send within 12 hours):
  "Hi {Name}, thanks again for accepting our offer. There's a short operational change that affects your start timing. We can offer a temporary 14-day emergency boarding path so you can start contributing earlier while we finalize logistics. This includes limited access, a mentor, and a clear review on day 14 to decide next steps. Please reply if you'd like to proceed and we will follow up with steps. — Aisha (People Ops)"

- Manager update (internal):
  "Heads-up: we're initiating emergency boarding for {Name} to cover {gap}. POC: {Aisha}. Access scope: limited. Mentor: {Mentor}. Please avoid granting production deploy rights unless approved by Security."

Security and legal notes:
- Always require explicit sign-off from Security for any elevation beyond read-only dashboards. Use the Security Exception template and attach to Jira HR-1982.
- Background checks must be in progress. If incomplete, document residual risks and get Legal approval for temporary access.
- Retain audit logs and apply auto-expiry on all temporary credentials.

Manager & Mentor responsibilities (concise):
- Manager: propose 1–2 small onboarding tickets; commit to 30–60 min/day mentorship for first week; attend day 14 decision sync.
- Mentor: create a 90-min repo walkthrough (record if possible); unblock tickets; ensure candidate knows runbooks for safe testing.

Failure modes and de-escalation steps:
- Candidate declines: close case, offer cooling-off plan and next steps for re-engagement.
- Compliance/legal flag: immediately revoke interactive access and escalate to Legal; preserve artifacts and notify manager.
- Hardware delay persists >14d: move candidate to contractor stipend or cloud-only path; communicate options.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Payroll edge cases for international candidates starting as emergency-boarded contractors? (Renee to consult finance).
- Template for auto-expiring IAM roles still lives in infra repo; make a lightweight PeopleOps wrapper (Miguel).
- Need metrics: track NPS for temporary boarding candidates and time-to-first-meaningful-commit. Add to Q1 people ops dashboard.

Quick links and references:
- Emergency IAM role template: github:infra/iam-templates#emergency-14d
- Onboarding kit checklist: confluence:Onboard/Kit-V2
- Incident reporting: #security-ops Slack channel

Appendix: short decision rubric for day-14
- Green: BG check cleared, mentor recommended continuation, candidate still interested -> convert to full onboarding.
- Yellow: BG pending but low risk, manager wants more time -> extend temporary path 7 days max with Legal sign-off.
- Red: BG failure or misalignment of expectations -> offboard with documented feedback and rehire policy note.

Notes to self (casual, keep):
- Keep emails short and empathetic. Candidates hate bureaucracy; transparency wins.
- Automate expiry as much as possible; manual offboarding is our biggest risk.
- Push this as an official mini-runbook into Confluence after iteration 1 with sample templates and baseline metrics.

Revision history:
- 2026-01-12 Aisha: initial draft and triage checklist.
- 2026-01-25 Miguel: added IAM automation TODOs and access matrix.
- 2026-02-03 Renee: added legal notes and payroll questions.
